page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / Sign on the dotted line
title: Sign on the dotted line
description:
It's time for Anna to develop Tip Top Trading's European marketing strategy but where should she begin? Her boss, Paul, doesn't have a clue so it's down to Anna to work out what to do. Listen in to find out what her plan is and how she sets out to manage the project of securing a deal with a French company.
This episode focuses on what to say when you need to develop a strategy for your business.
phrases: We've got to compete on price.
We need to price our rivals out of the market.
We need to corner the market.
We need to build good relationships with our customers.

listening_challenge.question: Paul tells Anna he wants to touch base, what does he mean?
listening_challenge.answer: To catch up and discuss how things are going.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Help, help!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Help us! We're locked in.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Oh dear. Do you remember that Tom and Anna are locked in the stationery cupboard? What are they going to do? And what will people say when they are discovered in there? I have a feeling we're about to find out…

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Goodness, what's that? Anna is that you? And is that you Tom?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes, help! We're locked in.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Don't panic, I've got the key. There. How on earth…

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: …it's not how it looks Denise. We were just… erm…

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: …just looking for envelopes.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Really?!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes, yes, really. The door slammed shut and locked from the inside when Tom walked in.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah, she's right. Just walked in, and shut the door and bang.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Hmm. Let's just keep it our little secret shall we. (Aside to Anna) I thought you had better taste Anna!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Ah there you are Anna, I need a word with you… Oh, you look like you've been caught doing something you shouldn't! Ha ha.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: …but I haven't.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Just joking Anna. Now could you step in to my office, we need to touch base about the European marketing strategy.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Are we playing baseball?!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: No Anna! Touch base. He wants to catch up with you, probably to see how you're getting on. Go on Anna, let's see what he has to say.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh I see. That door doesn't lock does it?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: No, I don't think so. Right Anna. Biscuit? These new peanut ones are quite nice. So how are things with the project?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, I've done some cold calling and have an order from a company in France.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: I see. Very impressive but have they signed on the dotted line yet?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: The dotted line?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Have they actually signed the contract yet?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, no, but…

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: …that's the problem. There's a rival company who's also targeting the European market called Tutti Fruity - and they'll do anything to steal our customers.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh I see.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: So, to keep our head above water, we need a clear strategy… and that's why I've put you in charge. So what shall we do?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: I've a feeling Paul hasn't a clue – that's why he wants you to come up with the ideas.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I think you're right – but I don't know what to say.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Tell him we need to price the rivals out of the market, that means offer the lowest prices so nobody wants to buy plastic fruit from our rivals. You could say that we need to corner the market, that means Tip Top Trading dominates the plastic fruit market.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh, thanks. That's very useful.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: So Anna, any thoughts?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Lots Paul. I think we've got to compete on price.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Oh yes?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: We need to price Tutti Fruity out of the market. We need to corner the market so that everyone knows we are the best choice for good quality, good value plastic fruit.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: I like it!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: And… and…

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Tell him we need to build good relationships with our customers – that means we give them good service.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: …we need to build good relationships with our customers. Talk to them regularly, send them gifts… go and meet them face to face.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Face to face? Yes, great idea – just what I was thinking. If we follow this strategy I reckon there could be a bonus for us all by Christmas.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Well done Anna. Very convincing. If you can put your ideas into practice you'll save the company. Let's remind ourselves of the words you used to create the European marketing strategy…

transcript.speaker: We've got to compete on price.
transcript.text:
We need to price the rivals out of the market.
We need to corner the market.
We need to build good relationships with our customers.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Well, things seem to be going well for Anna… or are they?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Anna! Anna! That man from France has called again and left a message. He's not happy this time. Something about us trying to rip them off!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: What? Rip them off?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: It means over charging them or giving them poor quality goods.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: That's not fair. I'm going to have to sort this out.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: That's it Anna – go and build a good relationship with your customer! Bye for now.
